description.narrative: Core support to a civil society organisation working with the protection of Palestinian rights to land and socio-economic development in East Jerusalem.
Kärnstöd till en civilsamhällesorganisation som arbetar med att skydda för palestinska landrättigheter i Östra Jerusalem.

Objective 1: Safeguarding the conditions for an agreed two state solution and the character of Jerusalem as the present home and future capital of the two peoples, while impeding unilateral and formal and de-facto annexation steps.
Objective 2: Protecting the individual and collective home of Palestinians in East Jerusalem including their physical and communal space, socio-economic rights and their right to the city.
Objective 3: Local and international target audiences are informed, mobilized and subsequently act with regard to on-the-ground developments that affect the current reality in Jerusalem and the prospect for a negotiated solution.

The cooperation partner has had some success with regards to preventing settlement expansion in Silwan, where the cooperation partner lawsuit against the Israeli government for funding a settler visitor center in the neighbourhood, led to a temporary injunction by the Jerusalem District Court. With regards to the planned Mount Scopus Slopes National Park (which would further entrench the settler presence in East Jerusalem and lead to loss of land for Palestinian neighbourhoods), The cooperation partner engagement led to a decrease of 100 dunams of the size of the park.
The focus of the cooperation partner under this strategic objective has been to follow-up and advocate for a fairer implementation of the East Jerusalem Second Five-year Investment Plan, which was adopted to make the municipal investments in Jerusalem less discriminatory and imbalanced.Overall, the investment plan has not been implemented in a satisfactory way. However, one success story is the progress of the health care sector where the health ministry team has worked extensively to advance goals, approving programs for early childhood health and strengthening community health services. This success reflect in part, sustained advocacy efforts by the civil society health coalition formed by cooperation partner and several partner organizations.
Another important development regards the Water supply in Kfar Aqab, which was drastically reduced by the Israeli authorities during the summer of 2024. The cooperation partner petitioned to the High Court demanding regular and continuous water supply for the neighborhood. Following the petition, the Water Authority toured the neighborhood and concluded that increased water supply was needed and that infrastructure work is planned to allow for a long-term increase in water supply to the neighborhood. The Court ruled that the State must update on measures taken to improve the situation.
In addition to the above tangible and direct results, the cooperation partner has continued to engaged in monitoring, reporting, and advocacy against the escalating demolitions in East Jerusalem. In particular, they reported on the severe escalation in restrictions on the ability of Palestinians to obtain building permits, and worked directly with local communities facing threats of collective displacement. In several neighborhoods in East Jerusalem, the cooperation partner is leading campaigns to support the struggle of the local communities to protect their homes. This include the organization of numerous tours, diplomatic briefings, articles and social media posts. In the specific case of the community of al-Walaja, the cooperation partner is assisting the residents in advancing an approved building plan and prevent home demolitions, and regular coordination meeting with community leaders are held.
What has changed for whom? Are the operations making a difference?
By and large, the situation for Palestinians in East Jerusalem has become more difficult during the period according to most parameters (e.g. building-permits, demolitions, land confiscation, access to holy sites, investments in public utilities and services, increase in municipal taxes despite receiving very few services). The Israeli government and the local municipality (whose deputy mayor is a settler in East Jerusalem) have continued to expand settlements, and several laws are currently being considered by the Knesset that would further diminish the Palestinian characteristic of East Jerusalem, including the "New Jerusalem Bill" which would expand the municipal border of Jerusalem to include settlements in the periphery, further shifting the demographic reality of the city in favour of Israelis, and ultimately making a two-state solution more difficult to realise.
It is important to see the work of the cooperation partner as part of the greater goal of promoting the long-term conditions for a negotiated two-state solution in accordance with international law, where Jerusalem and its status has a central role. Even marginal improvements, or small successes in preventing displacement can have an out-sized effect in the future.
Concretely, the efforts of the cooperation partner, as highlighted above, has limited the expansion of the settler visitor center in Silwan by 100 dunams (10 hectars). This is a success in of itself but should be seen as successfully countering the attempts of settlers to transform the Wadi Hilweh/City of David, to an exclusively Jewish area by, among other things, the politicization of archaeology.
The putative efforts of the Water Authority to increase the water supply in Kfar Aqab is also a success achieved due to the efforts of the cooperation partner. Even though concrete results remain to be seen, the conditions have been set for a fairer distribution of municipal services, making Jerusalem a more equitable city and will facilitate the lives of Palestinians. In the same vein, the advocacy efforts of the cooperation partner and its partners have led to a relatively satisfying implementation of the part of the East Jerusalem Second Five-year Investment Plan which relates to health care which is also facilitating continued Palestinian presence and resilience in East Jerusalem.
In conclusion, the Consulate General finds that the cooperation partner's activities improve the lives of Palestinian Jerusalemites at the individual and communal level, while also contributing to the long-term goal of ensuring the conditions for an agreed two state solution and the character of Jerusalem as the present home and future capital of the two peoples are safeguarded.
